title: Jazz trio at the Famous Door on Bourbon Street
summary: He played about a year, two nights a week, in a trio with Jeff Riddick and Raymond Boyk relieving the Girard and Dukes of Dixieland bands.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever work on Bourbon Street yourself here?

Once. I had one job, and it lasted about a year, at the Famous Door. Two nights a week, a jazz trio. We used to relieve... At that time, George Girard was one of the bands, and the Dukes of Dixieland was the other band at the Famous Door, and the union demanded, of course, they get a night off. Sure. And that would be a Sunday and a Monday, you see. So, when those bands were off, the club provided entertainment in the form of this jazz trio. And I was a member of that trio. It was Jeff Riddick, Raymond Boyk, and myself. And we would play at the intermissions when the six-piece band would be off at a stand, and we'd get up and play for twenty minutes out of an hour. And our biggest problem was trying to find something to do with ourselves, and at forty minutes, you know, we'd just have to sit there and listen to the other bands. Okay.
